info.title: IceScreen Touch API
info.summary: Control an iPhone or iPad from scripts through IceScreen Touch on the same Windows PC.
info.description:
IceScreen Touch mirrors an iPhone or iPad to a Windows PC and sends mouse input to the device as Bluetooth LE
HID touches. This automation API lets a script or an AI agent do the same with programmatic input: touch gestures
(tap, long press, swipe, path, pinch), keys and text, the home button, and low-level multi-touch over a
WebSocket. The version of this document is the version of the API (`apiVersion` in `GET /v1/status` is its
major number, `1`).

## Availability

* The API is **off by default**. The user switches it on in the app (Settings, "Automation API"). It listens on
  `127.0.0.1` only (never on `::1` or another address) on port 47821 by default; the user can choose another
  port (1024 to 65535, not the probe page's port 8000). A port that is in use is an error in the app, the app
  never looks for another one.
* The API is part of the purchased app (and of a build made from the source). While the app is in its trial, or while
  the Microsoft Store license cannot be checked, it
  is not started; if the license stops covering it while the API runs, every call answers `403`
  `purchase_required`, except `POST /v1/cancel` (a stop command always works).
* The API can only drive the one target device the app currently sends input to (see `PUT /v1/target`).

## Finding the API (connection discovery)

When the API is on, the app writes `api.json` (only the current Windows user can read it) and deletes it when
the API is switched off:

```json
{ "port": 47821, "token": "<43 characters>", "pid": 1234 }
```

* Normal install: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\IceScreenTouch\api.json`.
* Store (MSIX) install: the same file is redirected to
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Shin-plaster.IceScreenTouch_5c159ja95e6hm\LocalCache\Local\IceScreenTouch\api.json`
  when `%LOCALAPPDATA%\IceScreenTouch` did not exist yet; if that folder already existed (for example from a
  build of your own), the Store install uses it like a normal install.
* `pid` is the process that owns the port, so a client can check that it talks to IceScreen Touch (and that
  the process runs as the same Windows user, see the owner check in the API guide) before it sends the token.
* Clients are expected to look first at the environment variables `ICESCREENTOUCH_API` (for example
  `http://127.0.0.1:47821`) and `ICESCREENTOUCH_TOKEN`, then at `api.json`.

## Authentication and browser protection

* Every call except `GET /v1/openapi.json` and the WebSocket upgrade of `GET /v1/stream` carries
  `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token is 256 random bits as 43 Base64url characters; the user can copy
  or regenerate it in the app. Regenerating it makes the old one stop working at once (an open WebSocket is
  closed with 1008).
* A browser cannot set `Authorization` on a WebSocket, so the WebSocket takes the token in its first message
  (see `GET /v1/stream`).
* Any request with an `Origin` header is refused with `403` `forbidden_origin` (there is no CORS: scripts and
  command-line tools do not send `Origin`, web pages always do).
* The `Host` header must be `127.0.0.1:<port>` with the port of the API (protection against DNS rebinding;
  use the address `127.0.0.1`, not the name `localhost`), else `403` `forbidden_origin`.
* The checks run in this order: `Origin`, `Host`, token (`401` `unauthorized`, with
  `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`), route (`404` `not_found`, `405` `method_not_allowed` with an `Allow` header), then
  the request body.

## Requests and responses

* Success is `200` with a JSON body. Operations that return nothing answer `{}`. The one exception is
  `GET /v1/screenshot`, which answers an image (PNG or JPEG) with the details in `X-IceScreenTouch-*` headers.
* Errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with the machine-readable extension member `code` (see
  the `Problem` schema). `type` is always `about:blank`; `detail` is a sentence for a person and never contains
  your data.
* A body is JSON in UTF-8 with `Content-Type: application/json` and at most **64 KB**. A body that is not valid for
  the endpoint is `400` `invalid_request`: unknown members are refused, missing required members are refused,
  numbers must be JSON numbers (not strings), and a body is required where the endpoint takes one.
* Every response has `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
* An operation answers only **after** it has finished on the device (a swipe answers after the finger lifted).

## Operations: one at a time, limited in time

* Only **one operation at a time**. A touch, key, home, `PUT /v1/rotation`, `PUT /v1/target` or a WebSocket
  session that is running makes every other operation answer `409` `busy`; the API never queues. `GET
  /v1/status`, `GET /v1/rotation`, `GET /v1/screenshot` and `GET /v1/openapi.json` are not operations and always work. While the
  probe (measurement) page of the app is running, operations are `409` `busy` too.
* No operation takes longer than **60 seconds** (the sum of holds, durations, intervals and the last `t` of a
  path), else `400` `invalid_request`.
* A touch is held at least **70 ms** (a shorter `holdMs` of a tap or long press is raised to 70); frames of a
  moving finger go out every 16 ms. A finger is always lifted at its last position.
* `POST /v1/cancel` stops the running operation (the fingers and keys are lifted; the stopped request answers
  `499` `cancelled`).

## The user has priority

The person at the PC can always take over the mirror window. When they use it (mouse press on the picture,
wheel, the keys that go to the device, Home, rotate), a running operation is stopped, every finger is lifted
and every key is released: a REST call answers `409` `user_interrupted`, a WebSocket stream gets an
`interrupted` event with reason `user` and is closed. For one second after the user's last input (and while they
hold the mouse or a key), a new operation is refused with `409` `user_active`. The API never resumes by itself:
the client decides whether to try again.

## Coordinate spaces

Every position has a space, `space` (default `screen`):

| space | meaning | needs the picture |
|---|---|---|
| `screen` | The screen **as it is seen now**, normalized to 0..1 (0,0 top left, 1,1 bottom right). Landscape means a wide screen. The app undoes the rotation. | yes |
| `pixel` | Pixels of a screenshot. `ref: { "width": W, "height": H }`, the size of that screenshot, is **required**. x is 0..W, y is 0..H. | yes |
| `device` | The digitizer's own portrait frame, 0..1, never rotated. | no |

* A position outside the range (below 0, above 1 or above the `ref` size, or not a number) is `400`
  `invalid_request`.
* `screen` and `pixel` need the picture of the device (to know whether it is portrait or landscape). Without
  it (the receiver window is closed or minimized) the call is `409` `no_picture`.
* A `pixel` request whose `ref` has the opposite orientation (wide versus tall) from the current picture means
  the device rotated since the screenshot: `409` `picture_changed`. Take a new screenshot. A square `ref` is
  never refused.
* The **left or right side of a landscape screen cannot be detected** by the app. The assumed rotation is in
  `GET /v1/status` (`rotation`); if it is wrong, correct it with `PUT /v1/rotation` (saved, like `Ctrl+R`
  in the app). The same holds for an upside-down portrait screen (180).

## Notes on the device

* Touch input only arrives if **Zoom** (Accessibility) is on in the device.
* Typing sends keys of a **US keyboard**. Characters without a key (Japanese, emoji) cannot be typed directly;
  they are skipped and reported.
* The API cannot know whether the device is locked and does not stop input to a passcode screen.

servers.description: The app on the same PC. Only 127.0.0.1 is served.

port.description: The port chosen in the app (default 47821). The connection file `api.json` has it.

tags.name: status
tags.description: Read the state of the app and the device.

tags.name: settings
tags.description: Change what the app assumes (target device, rotation).

tags.name: touch
tags.description: Touch gestures of one or two fingers.

tags.name: keys
tags.description: Keyboard input and the home button.

get.summary: State of the app, the devices and the picture
get.description: Not an operation: it works while another operation runs (`operating` tells whether one does).

put.summary: Choose the device that gets the input
put.description:
Sets the device that touches and keys go to (`null` = automatic). A device id is one of `devices[].id` of
`GET /v1/status`; an unknown id is `400` `invalid_request`.

409.description:
`not_running` (the mirroring session is not running) or `busy` (another operation, a stream or the probe
page is running).

get.description: Not an operation: it works while another operation runs.

put.description:
The app cannot tell the two landscape directions (90 or 270) or an upside-down portrait (180) from the
picture, so it assumes one. This corrects the assumption (saved, like `Ctrl+R` in the app). At least one of
`landscape` and `portrait` is required; the one that is left out stays. It is an operation (`busy` while
another runs) but needs no picture and no connected device. Answers the rotations now in force.

409.description: `busy`: another operation, a stream or the probe page is running.

post.summary: Tap (one finger, once or several times)
post.description:
Puts one finger down at the position, holds it for `holdMs` (at least 70) and lifts it; repeated `count`
times with `intervalMs` between a lift and the next touch (at least 25). The total
(`count` x hold + (`count` - 1) x interval) is at most 60 seconds.

screen.summary: Tap the middle of the screen

pixel.summary: Double tap at a screenshot pixel

post.description: One finger held at the position for `holdMs` (default 800, at least 70).

post.summary: Swipe or drag with one finger
post.description:
The finger goes down at `from`, waits there `holdBeforeMs` (a long press before the drag, for example to
reorder icons), moves in a straight line to `to` in `durationMs` (a frame every 16 ms), waits there
`holdAfterMs` (stops the scrolling momentum) and lifts at `to`. `holdBeforeMs` + `durationMs` +
`holdAfterMs` is at most 60 seconds.

post.summary: Drag one finger along any path
post.description:
One finger follows `points`; each point has `t`, the milliseconds since the finger went down (not decreasing
from point to point). A frame goes out every 16 ms at the position interpolated linearly between the points;
the last frame is the last point, then the finger lifts there. If the first `t` is above 0 the finger waits at
the first point until then. The last `t` is at most 60000 (60 seconds). Use it to draw curves without a
WebSocket.

Two fingers are placed side by side horizontally around `center`, each `radius` away from it, and the radius
goes from `startRadius` to `endRadius` in `durationMs` (at least 70 ms in all). The radius is a fraction of
the screen's **short side** (in `device` space: of the digitizer's x axis, which spans the device's short
side). `endRadius` larger than `startRadius` spreads the fingers (zoom in), smaller pinches them together. A
finger that would leave the screen at the start or the end is `400` `invalid_request`.

Presses a key of a US keyboard for `holdMs` (default 30; unlike a touch it is not raised to 70) and releases
it. The names are the **device's**: the app does not translate PC key layouts (`cmd` is the device's Command
key, not the PC's Ctrl).

* Characters: `a` to `z` (lower case), `0` to `9` and the unshifted US symbols `` - = [ ] \ ; ' , . / ` ``.
  A character that needs Shift on its own (`A`, `!`) is refused: send the base key with the `shift` modifier.
* Names (not case sensitive): `Enter`, `Escape`, `Backspace`, `Tab`, `Space`, `Delete`, `ArrowUp`,
  `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Home`, `End`, `F1` to `F12`.
* Modifiers (`modifiers`): `cmd`, `shift`, `option`, `ctrl`.
* `Home` is the keyboard key of that name. The device's home **button** is `POST /v1/home`.

Needs the keyboard in the published HID map (`409` `no_keyboard` otherwise). Examples: select all
`{ "key": "a", "modifiers": ["cmd"] }`; switch the input method `{ "key": "Space", "modifiers": ["ctrl"] }`.

post.summary: Type a text, one character at a time
post.description:
Types `text` on a US keyboard, a character every `intervalMs` (plus about 30 ms of key hold; Shift costs
about 30 ms more). At most 1000 characters, and the estimated time must stay within 60 seconds (else
`400` `invalid_request`; split the text into several requests). New lines are typed as Enter and tabs as Tab.

Characters that have no key on a US keyboard (Japanese, emoji, accented letters) are **not typed**; they are
returned in `skipped`. Japanese cannot be typed directly: switch the device to its "Japanese - Romaji"
keyboard (for example with `ctrl` + `Space`), type the romaji and confirm with the keys.

Needs the keyboard in the published HID map (`409` `no_keyboard` otherwise).

Sends the home key (Consumer Control "Menu") of the device. Needs the home button in the published HID map
(`409` `no_home_button` otherwise). No body.

Ends the operation or WebSocket stream that is running: every finger is lifted and every key released. The
stopped REST request answers `499` `cancelled`; a stream gets an `interrupted` event with reason `cancelled`
and is closed. Answers at once; `cancelled` tells whether something was running. No body. This call works even when
the license does not cover the API (a stop command always works).

get.summary: A picture of the device screen
get.description:
The picture of the device as the receiver window shows it: exactly the rectangle that `GET /v1/status` reports as
`picture` (the black bars of the window are left out), as a PNG or a JPEG. The image is made from the receiver window
alone, so other windows (notifications, overlays) do not appear in it. For about 2 seconds after a screenshot is taken, a colored border
(usually yellow) is shown around the receiver window; the border is not in the image. If Windows' capture is temporarily
unavailable (rare), a screenshot may be taken without the border.

* The image size follows the **size of the receiver window**, not the resolution of the device. Use the size of
  the screenshot you took as `ref` when you point at it with `space: "pixel"`.
* `maxSize` only shrinks (the longest side becomes `maxSize`, the aspect stays); it never enlarges. Without it the
  image has the size of the picture. The header `X-IceScreenTouch-Source-Size` always has the size before shrinking.
* The image has no transparency.
* Not an operation: it takes no part in the one-operation-at-a-time rule, so it also works while an operation or a
  WebSocket stream runs; it never answers `busy`. It sends nothing to the device.
* At most **10 screenshots in any 1 second**, counted over all clients. The 11th gets `429` `rate_limited` with
  `Retry-After: 1`. Only requests that passed the query check count (also when they are then answered `not_running`
  or `no_picture`); a request refused with `429` does not count. Too many screenshots in progress at once are also
  answered `429` `rate_limited`.
* Checks in this order, after the common ones (`Origin`, `Host`, token): the license (`403` `purchase_required`), the
  query (`400` `invalid_request`), the rate limit (`429`), `409` `not_running`, `409` `no_picture` (no picture: the
  receiver window is closed, minimized, on another virtual desktop or not found, or it could not be read).
* The query parameter names are case-sensitive and the values are exact: `format` is `png` or `jpeg` in lower case;
  `maxSize` and `quality` are plain decimal digits. An unknown or repeated parameter, a value out of range, and
  `quality` with `format=png` are `400` `invalid_request`.

parameters.name: maxSize
parameters.description:
The longest side of the image in pixels. The image is shrunk to it when it is larger and is not touched when it
is smaller or equal. Without it the image keeps the size of the picture.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: The JPEG quality. Only with `format=jpeg` (with `png` it is `400` `invalid_request`).

200.description:
The image. The body is the file (`Content-Type` is `image/png` or `image/jpeg`); the headers say how the app saw
the picture when it was taken.

X-IceScreenTouch-Orientation.description: `portrait`, or `landscape` when the picture is wider than tall (a square one is `portrait`).

X-IceScreenTouch-Rotation.description: The rotation the app assumes for that orientation (see `GET /v1/rotation`), in degrees.

X-IceScreenTouch-Source-Size.description: The size of the picture before `maxSize` shrank it, `<width>x<height>` in pixels, for example `1179x2556`.

409.description:
`not_running` (the mirroring session is not running) or `no_picture` (the receiver window is closed, minimized,
on another virtual desktop or not found, or it could not be read).

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: there is no picture of the device

get.description:
Upgrades the connection to a WebSocket (`Upgrade: websocket`; response `101`) for low-level input: put one or
two fingers down, move them, lift them, press and release keys, all in real time. OpenAPI cannot describe a
WebSocket; the protocol is described here, and the messages are the schemas `StreamClientMessage` and
`StreamEvent` in this document. Messages are JSON in **text** frames (a binary frame closes the connection
with 1003), at most **4 KB** each (a larger one closes it with 1009).

## Handshake and authentication

There is no `Authorization` header (a browser cannot set one on a WebSocket) and the `Origin` and `Host`
checks of the API still apply before the upgrade (`403` `forbidden_origin`). The **first message** must be
`{ "op": "auth", "token": "<token>" }`, within **2 seconds** of the upgrade. A wrong or late first message is
answered with an `error` event (`unauthorized`) and the close code 1008.

After a good `auth` the stream opens a **session**: it behaves like a running operation, so every other
operation answers `409` `busy` while the stream is open (`GET /v1/status`, `GET /v1/rotation` and the
specification still work), the user's mouse and keys are held back from the device, and the same preconditions
as for touches apply (session running, device connected, user not active). The server sends
`{ "ev": "ready", "api": 1 }`. If the session cannot be opened the server sends an `error` event with the
reason (`purchase_required`, `busy`, `user_active`, `not_connected`, `not_running`) and closes
(see the close codes). At most 4 streams can be connected at once, but only one can hold the session; beyond 4
the upgrade itself is refused with `409` `busy`. A request that is not a WebSocket upgrade is `400`
`invalid_request`.

## Messages from the client

Every message below except `auth` and `ping` has a number `seq` (an integer, 0 or more) that the answer
repeats. Members that an `op` does not take are refused (`error`, `invalid_request`). A message that is not a
valid JSON object of this API is answered with an `error` event without `seq`; the stream stays open.

| op | members | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `auth` | `token` | First message only. |
| `down` | `seq`, `contacts`, optional `space` (default `screen`), optional `ref` | Puts the listed fingers down (a finger that is already down moves). `space` and `ref` apply to the following `move` messages too. |
| `move` | `seq`, `contacts` | Moves fingers that are down (each must be down first). |
| `up` | `seq` | Lifts every finger at its last position. |
| `key` | `seq`, `key`, optional `modifiers`, `down` | Presses (`down: true`) or releases (`false`) a key; names and modifiers as in `POST /v1/keys/press`. At most 6 keys can be down at once. |
| `ping` | none | Answered with `{ "ev": "pong" }`; keeps the stream alive. |

`contacts` has 1 or 2 entries `{ "id": 0 or 1, "x", "y" }` (unique ids; the digitizer has two points). The
coordinates are those of `space` (see the coordinate spaces in the description of this API); the picture and
the rotation are read again for every message, so a rotation or a new picture is honoured.

## Messages from the server

| ev | members | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ready` | `api` | The stream is open. |
| `ack` | `seq` | The message with this `seq` was carried out (sent to the device). |
| `error` | `seq` (when known), `code`, `detail` | The message was refused and did nothing. `code` is a code of the `Problem` schema (`invalid_request`, `not_connected`, `no_picture`, `picture_changed`, `no_keyboard`, ...). The stream stays open, except where a close code is listed below. |
| `interrupted` | `reason` | `user` (the user took over), `cancelled` (`POST /v1/cancel` or the server stops) or `session_ended` (the mirroring session ended): everything was lifted and released and the stream is closed. `idle`: see the dead-man below; the stream stays open. |
| `pong` | none | The answer to `ping`. |

## Timing and the dead-man

* `move` messages are applied at most once every 16 ms: moves that arrive in between are merged into the last
  position and acknowledged as applied (every `seq` gets its `ack`).
* **Dead-man**: while a finger or key is down, if no message arrives for **1 second**, everything is lifted
  and released and the server sends `{ "ev": "interrupted", "reason": "idle" }`. The stream stays open. To hold
  a finger still, send `ping` regularly.
* More than 1000 frames in a second close the stream (1008, `error` `rate_limited`). Real use is 60 to 125 a
  second.
* When the stream ends for any reason (a client close, a broken connection, the user, the server) every finger
  is lifted and every key released first, then the session is given up.

## Close codes

| code | when |
|---|---|
| 1000 | The client closed the stream; or the user, `POST /v1/cancel` or the end of the mirroring session stopped it (an `interrupted` event came first). |
| 1001 | The app is shutting down; or the session could not be opened because the request was cancelled. |
| 1003 | A binary frame. |
| 1008 | Authentication failed or timed out; the token was regenerated; the API is not covered by the license (`purchase_required`); too many messages per second. An `error` event comes first. |
| 1009 | A message larger than 4 KB. |
| 1011 | An internal error (for example a failed Bluetooth write); an `error` event (`internal_error`) comes first. |
| 1013 | Try again later: the session could not be opened because of `busy`, `user_active`, `not_connected` or `not_running`. An `error` event with that code comes first. |

Example session:

```
-> { "op": "auth", "token": "..." }
<- { "ev": "ready", "api": 1 }
-> { "op": "down", "seq": 1, "space": "screen", "contacts": [{ "id": 0, "x": 0.2, "y": 0.5 }] }
<- { "ev": "ack", "seq": 1 }
-> { "op": "move", "seq": 2, "contacts": [{ "id": 0, "x": 0.8, "y": 0.5 }] }
<- { "ev": "ack", "seq": 2 }
-> { "op": "up", "seq": 3 }
<- { "ev": "ack", "seq": 3 }
```

101.description: Switching protocols. The WebSocket is open.

400.description: `invalid_request`: the request is not a WebSocket upgrade.

403.description: `forbidden_origin`: an `Origin` header is present, or `Host` is not allowed.

get.description:
The specification (the same document as this file, in JSON). It needs no token; the `Origin` and `Host`
checks still apply.

403.description: `forbidden_origin`: an `Origin` header is present, or `Host` is not allowed.

bearerAuth.description:
The token of `api.json` (or `ICESCREENTOUCH_TOKEN`), 43 Base64url characters. Sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

BadRequest.description: `invalid_request`: the body, a range, a limit or a name is wrong. `detail` says which (never the value).

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: position is outside the screen (x and y must be in 0..1)

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized`: the bearer token is missing or wrong.

Forbidden.description:
`forbidden_origin` (an `Origin` header is present, or `Host` is not `127.0.0.1:<port>`)
or `purchase_required` (the license does not cover the API).

ConflictTouch.description:
The operation cannot run now: `busy` (another operation, a stream or the probe page is running), `not_running`
(the mirroring session is not running), `user_active` (the user used the mirror within the last second),
`not_connected` (the target device has not subscribed to the touch reports), `no_picture` (`screen` and `pixel`
need the picture), `picture_changed` (a `pixel` request whose `ref` has the opposite orientation of the
picture) or `user_interrupted` (the user took over while it ran; everything was lifted).

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: another operation or session is running

ConflictKey.description:
The operation cannot run now: `busy`, `not_running`, `user_active`, `not_connected`, `no_keyboard` (the
published HID map has no keyboard) or `user_interrupted`.

Cancelled.description:
`cancelled`: `POST /v1/cancel` (or the client going away) ended the operation. Every finger was lifted and
every key released.

RateLimited.description:
`rate_limited`: more than 10 screenshots in one second (over all clients), or too many screenshots in progress at once. Try again after the time in
`Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next try. Always `1`.

InternalError.description:
`internal_error`: an unexpected failure inside the app (for example a failed Bluetooth write). The detail is
generic.

Problem.description:
An error, RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. The meaning is in `code`.

| code | HTTP | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_request` | 400 | The body, a range, a limit or a name is wrong. |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | The token is missing or wrong. |
| `forbidden_origin` | 403 | The `Origin` header is present, or `Host` is not allowed. |
| `purchase_required` | 403 | The license does not cover the API (trial, expired). |
| `not_found` | 404 | No such endpoint. |
| `method_not_allowed` | 405 | The endpoint does not accept that HTTP method (`Allow` lists the ones it does). |
| `not_running` | 409 | The mirroring session is not running. |
| `not_connected` | 409 | The target device has not subscribed to the HID reports. |
| `no_picture` | 409 | There is no picture (the receiver window is closed or minimized, or it could not be read) and the request needs one. |
| `picture_changed` | 409 | A `pixel` request refers to a screenshot of the opposite orientation: the device rotated since. |
| `busy` | 409 | Another operation, a WebSocket stream or the probe page is running. |
| `user_interrupted` | 409 | The user used the mirror; everything was lifted. |
| `user_active` | 409 | The user used the mirror within the last second, or holds the mouse or a key. |
| `no_keyboard` | 409 | The published HID map has no keyboard. |
| `no_home_button` | 409 | The published HID map has no home button. |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | More than 10 screenshots in one second, or too many screenshots in progress at once (`Retry-After: 1` for both), or too many messages per second on a WebSocket stream (it is closed). |
| `cancelled` | 499 | `POST /v1/cancel` (or the client going away) ended the operation. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | An unexpected failure inside the app. |

detail.description: A sentence for a person. Never contains positions, keys, text or the token.

examples.title: Conflict
examples.detail: the user used the mirror a moment ago

Empty.description: The body of an operation that returns nothing.

apiVersion.description: The major version of the API (1).

bleState.description: A short description of the Bluetooth state, for example `advertising` or `connected`.

targetDeviceId.description: The device that gets the input (`null` when there is none).

receiver.description: The AirPlay receiver the picture comes from (`null` when there is none).

picture.description: The picture of the device as the receiver window shows it (`null` when there is none).

operating.description: An API operation or stream is running.

subscribed.description: The device subscribed to the touch reports (it can receive input).

Picture.description:
The rectangle of the device's picture in the receiver window (black bars excluded), in PC pixels. The width
and height are not the device's resolution.

isLandscape.description: Wider than tall. A square counts as portrait.

Rotation.description: The rotations of the device the app assumes, in degrees.

landscape.description: Used when the picture is wide.

portrait.description: Used when the picture is tall.

skipped.description: The characters that have no key on a US keyboard (not typed). Empty when all were typed.

cancelled.description: True when an operation or stream was running and was told to stop; false when nothing ran.

Space.description:
The coordinate space of the positions (not case sensitive): `screen` (0..1 of the screen as seen now),
`pixel` (pixels of a screenshot; needs `ref`) or `device` (0..1 of the digitizer's portrait frame).

PixelRef.description: The size of the screenshot a `pixel` position refers to.

Point.description: A position in the space of the request.

deviceId.description: The device id, or `null` for automatic. The member must be present.

RotationRequest.description: At least one of the two members.

holdMs.description: How long the finger stays down. A value below 70 is raised to 70.

intervalMs.description: The pause between a lift and the next tap. A value below 25 is raised to 25.

holdMs.description: How long the finger stays down (at most 60000). A value below 70 is raised to 70.

durationMs.description: The time to move from `from` to `to`.

holdBeforeMs.description: The finger waits at `from` this long first (a long press before the drag).

holdAfterMs.description: The finger waits at `to` this long before the lift (stops the momentum).

t.description: Milliseconds since the finger went down; not decreasing from point to point; at most 60000.

startRadius.description: Half the distance between the fingers at the start, as a fraction of the screen's short side.

endRadius.description: Half the distance between the fingers at the end, as a fraction of the screen's short side.

durationMs.description: The time from start to end (the whole gesture lasts at least 70 ms).

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held while the key is pressed.

holdMs.description: How long the key stays down.

text.description:
The text, at most 1000 characters (UTF-16 code units). Its estimated typing time must be at most 60
seconds.

intervalMs.description: The pause after each typed character.

StreamContact.description: One finger of a `down` or `move` message.

id.description: The contact id (the digitizer has two points).

x.description: Horizontal position in the space of the last `down`.

y.description: Vertical position in the space of the last `down`.

StreamClientMessage.description:
A message from the client to `GET /v1/stream`, a JSON object in a text frame. `op` selects the kind; see
the description of `GET /v1/stream` for the members each kind takes. Messages that are not valid are
answered with an `error` event.

oneOf.title: auth
oneOf.description: The first message, within 2 seconds of the upgrade.

down.description: True to press, false to release.

StreamSeq.description: A number chosen by the client; the `ack` or `error` for the message repeats it.

StreamContacts.description: One or two fingers; the ids must be unique.

StreamEvent.description: A message from the server on `GET /v1/stream`, a JSON object in a text frame. `ev` selects the kind.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: The message was refused and did nothing.

seq.description: The `seq` of the refused message, when it had a valid one.

reason.description:
`user`, `cancelled` and `session_ended` end the stream (everything was lifted and released). `idle`
(the dead-man) lifted and released everything but the stream stays open.
